chunks: That day people will proceed separately to be shown their deeds.

key_terms.يَوْمَئِذٍ: That day (referring to the Day of Judgment)

ai.seo_question: What does it mean when people are described as 'ash-tatan' (separate groups) on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the term 'ashtatan' (dispersed) is interpreted not merely as physical scattering but as a categorization based on the weight of one's deeds, reflecting the principle of 'Taqsim' (division) of humanity into believers and disbelievers. This separation serves as the immediate precursor to the detailed presentation of the 'Kitab' (Record of Deeds), emphasizing that every minor action, whether good or evil, will be individually witnessed and accounted for by Allah. The verse underscores the justice of God, where the public display of deeds removes any ambiguity regarding individual responsibility.
